ratings_why.fun: Hold or run is a real choice every turn, and watching aged shelf goods march out under Grisel is a satisfying board to grow; a few cards (Tibby, Fence) are flat beside it.
ratings_why.distinct: 8 because no tribe today touches the shop: a persistent shelf of any tribe's units, aged, burned, auctioned and fielded as copies, plays unlike anything in the lobby or a generic auto-battler.

verdict_why: Two cards still leave a player guessing (Nyx's spell on the shelf, Tibby with no neighbour); fix those wordings and it can settle.

points.text: Officer Nyx: a Seized spell's place on the shelf is unstated. Does it take one of the 3 places, can it be pushed out, aged by Bond Clerk or burned by the Stoker? Say it takes a place and only units gain stats.
Tibby Slick: if the attacker has no unit beside it, does the hit land on Tibby normally or fizzle, and is the 'first time' used up? Add one clause.
The Auctioneer, Grisel and the full-shelf push all read 'oldest', so show the shelf in arrival order with a small turns-held count on each unit.
Keeper of the Stilt House reads cleanly, but the triple-from-shelf moment deserves its own animation: the herons stamp three seals together.
Gammer Eelby is plain gold text; a fence could instead sell your Contraband back to the shop for others to see, a fresher hook in the same slot.

standouts.why: Grisel turns the shelf into the board's second row; the fantasy of seized goods fighting for the law reads at once.
Honest Ned, informing on your own crew to launder it, is the smuggling joke done as a mechanic, and it reads in one line.
The Customs House auction where the otters profit is the seed's best gag, and it says exactly what it does.

weakest.why: Tibby's redirect is the only fiddly combat text in the tribe and has nothing to do with the shelf.
Gammer Eelby is a gold rider; it does its job but adds no picture.
Narrows Sentry is a plain count-the-shelf buff, a lesser Wenna.

flags.note: How a Seized spell sits on the shelf is not written.
Grisel's Contraband copies plus Wenna and Nan, or a shelved Wenna, can stack very high.
Dunmore with Ned and Squacco makes a several-times-a-turn replay loop, bounded only by gold.
